displayedInputs.question:
In the figure, \(ABCD\) is a square of side length \(1.\) The rectangles \(JKHG\) and \(EBCF\) are congruent. What is \(BE?\)

[Figure 1](attached-image-1)

In \(\triangle ABC,\) \(D\) is a point on side \(\overline{AC}\) such that \(BD=DC\) and \(\angle BCD\) measures \(70^\circ.\) What is the degree measure of \(\angle ADB?\)

[Figure 1](attached-image-2)

Rectangle \(ABCD\) and right triangle \(DCE\) have the same area. They are joined to form a trapezoid, as shown. What is \(DE?\)

[Figure 1](attached-image-3)

The circumference of the circle with center \(O\) is divided into \(12\) equal arcs, marked the letters \(A\) through \(L\) as seen below. What is the number of degrees in the sum of the angles \(x\) and \(y?\)

[Figure 1](attached-image-4)

Rectangle \(ABCD\) has sides \(CD=3\) and \(DA=5.\) A circle of radius \(1\) is centered at \(A,\) a circle of radius \(2\) is centered at \(B,\) and a circle of radius \(3\) is centered at \(C.\) Which of the following is closest to the area of the region inside the rectangle but outside all three circles?

[Figure 1](attached-image-5)

A straight one-mile stretch of highway, \(40\) feet wide, is closed. Robert rides his bike on a path composed of semicircles as shown. If he rides at \(5\) miles per hour, how many hours will it take to cover the one-mile stretch?

Note: \(1\) mile = \(5280\) feet

[Figure 1](attached-image-6)

Ann made a \(3\)-step staircase using \(18\) toothpicks as shown in the figure. How many toothpicks does she need to add to complete a \(5\)-step staircase?

[Figure 1](attached-image-7)

The diagram below shows the circular face of a clock with radius \(20\) cm and a circular disk with radius \(10\) cm externally tangent to the clock face at \(12\) o’clock. The disk has an arrow painted on it, initially pointing in the upward vertical direction. Let the disk roll clockwise around the clock face. At what point on the clock face will the disk be tangent when the arrow is next pointing in the upward vertical direction?

[Figure 1](attached-image-8)

mappings.rationale: Congruence makes the tilted rectangle's side lengths BE and 1. Its perpendicular sides and the square's boundaries give projection relationships, obtainable through similar right triangles or trigonometry.
mappings.answerReason: Let w=BE, a=JA and b=AG. Corner-triangle similarity gives EK=wa and EJ=wb, hence b+wa=1 and a+w(1+b)=1. Also a²+b²=1. Since a>0, a²=(1-b)(1+b)=wa(1+b) gives a=w(1+b), so a=1/2. Thus b=sqrt(3)/2 and w=(1-b)/a=2-sqrt(3).

mappings.rationale: The equal sides BD and DC give equal base angles in triangle BCD. The requested angle is an exterior angle of that triangle.
mappings.answerReason: BD=DC implies ∠DBC=∠BCD=70°. Since DA extends DC, ∠ADB equals the sum of the two remote interior angles: 70°+70°=140°.

mappings.rationale: Equating the rectangle's area with the right triangle's area determines CE using their common height DC. The Pythagorean theorem then determines DE.
mappings.answerReason: The rectangle has area 6×5=30 and DC=5. Therefore 5×CE/2=30, giving CE=12. The right triangle then gives DE=sqrt(5²+12²)=13.

mappings.rationale: Twelve equal arcs give central-angle increments of 30°. The marked angles can be found using equal-radius triangles, or as inscribed angles because A, O and G are collinear.
mappings.answerReason: Arc AE spans four increments, so ∠AOE=120° and x=(180°-120°)/2=30°. Arc GI spans two increments, so ∠GOI=60° and y=(180°-60°)/2=60°. Their sum is 90°.

mappings.rationale: Inside the rectangle, each circle contributes a quarter-disk. Their interiors do not overlap, so their sector areas can be subtracted from the rectangle's area.
mappings.answerReason: AB=3=1+2 and BC=5=2+3, so the adjacent circles are externally tangent; the circles centered at A and C are disjoint. The uncovered area is 15-(π/4)(1²+2²+3²)=15-7π/2≈4.004, closest to 4.0.

mappings.rationale: Each semicircle's arc length is π/2 times its forward diameter. Summing these diameters over the highway stretch gives the riding distance, which is divided by speed.
mappings.answerReason: The semicircle diameters together span one mile, so the total arc length is π/2 miles. At 5 miles per hour, the time is (π/2)/5=π/10 hours.

mappings.rationale: The task requires the relationship between orbital motion and a disk's absolute rotation during external rolling. Arc lengths and rotation properties support the calculation, but neither represents the required no-slip rolling relationship.
mappings.answerReason: Under no-slip external rolling, an orbital angle θ produces disk rotation (20/10)θ relative to the line of centers, plus θ from that line's own turning. Thus the absolute rotation is 3θ. Its first 360° return occurs at θ=120° clockwise, placing the tangency at 4 o'clock.
